title: Is Your Gaming PC Ready for GTA 6? Best ABS Gaming Desktops to Consider
summary: GTA 6 arrives on consoles November 19, 2026, with no PC date announced. Here is how I would judge whether a gaming desktop is ready for it anyway.
body_markdown:
Let me get the awkward part out of the way. As of September 2026, there is no announced PC version of Grand Theft Auto VI. The game is dated for 19 November 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and Series S, and Rockstar has not scheduled a Windows release.


So any article promising you the GTA 6 system requirements is making them up. What I can do is something more useful: look at how Rockstar has handled PC before, work out what that implies about timing, and describe what a desktop needs to be in good shape when the port does arrive.


## What We Actually Know


Rockstar’s recent pattern is consoles first, PC later, with a real gap. Grand Theft Auto V launched on consoles on 17 September 2013 and reached Windows on 14 April 2015 — about nineteen months. Red Dead Redemption 2 launched on consoles on 26 October 2018 and arrived on Windows on 5 November 2019, roughly twelve months.


Two data points are not a schedule, and Rockstar has said nothing about GTA 6 on PC. But if the pattern held, a PC release would land somewhere in the year or so after the console launch. That is the window I would plan around, and it changes what “ready” means — you are buying for late 2027 hardware expectations, not for November 2026.


## Who Makes These Machines


If you are buying a machine to keep for a few years, the builder is part of the decision. ABS has been doing this since 1990, when Fred Chang started it in Southern California as Always Better Service, a direct-mail computer company. It is a Newegg subsidiary now, based in Diamond Bar, California, and Newegg relaunched the brand on 1 October 2020 as Advanced Battlestations with a gaming focus.


The reason it belongs in an article about being ready for something that has not shipped yet is the build approach. ABS assembles in-house from name-brand retail components, so the upgrade path is an ordinary one: a bigger drive, a second memory kit, eventually a different graphics card, all standard parts on standard boards. Gamers Nexus tested the ABS Challenger ALI521 in 2021 and called it one of the most impressive prebuilts it had tried. The current range is in the[ABS brand store](https://www.newegg.com/ABS/BrandStore/ID-8484?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_is-your-gaming-pc-ready-for-gta-6) on Newegg.


## Step 1: Look at Video Memory First


Big open-world games are texture-hungry, and the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X each have 16GB of unified memory shared between CPU and GPU. Ports tend to reflect the memory budget the developers actually had.


That makes 8GB the number I would be cautious about. It is fine today at 1080p, and it will probably still work in a demanding 2027 release with settings turned down. But it is the spec most likely to force compromises, and video memory is the one thing you cannot add to a graphics card later. 12GB is the sensible floor for 1440p; 16GB is what I would want for anything above that.


## Step 2: Do Not Underestimate the Processor


GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2 are both CPU-heavy in ways that surprised people at launch — dense traffic, large simulated crowds, long draw distances. Those are the workloads where a processor with a large cache tends to hold its frame rate more steadily than one with more raw clock speed.


If you are choosing between spending on the card and spending on the chip for a game like this, I would not put everything into the card.


## Step 3: Check the Drive


Rockstar’s last two open-world releases were very large installs, and there is no reason to expect the next one to be smaller. A 1TB drive with an operating system and a few current titles on it will not have room. This is the cheapest part of getting ready and the one people leave until the week of release.


## The Machines I Would Consider


96MB of cache, 16GB of video memory, 2TB of storage. Ticks all three boxes.


The[ABS Stratos II Ruby with the Ryzen 7 9800X3D and RX 9070 XT](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16883362053?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_is-your-gaming-pc-ready-for-gta-6) is the one that satisfies every point above without argument. The processor is eight cores and sixteen threads with 96MB of L3 from second-generation 3D V-Cache, at 120W on Socket AM5. The card is 64 compute units and 4,096 stream processors with 16GB of GDDR6 on a 256-bit bus at 304W. There is 32GB of DDR5-6000, 2TB of M.2 storage, an 850W 80+ Gold supply and a 240mm liquid cooler on a GIGABYTE B850 board.


16GB of video memory and DDR5-6400 in a mid-range build. The memory choices are the point.


A tier down, the[ABS Cyclone Aqua with the Core i7-14700F and RTX 5060 Ti 16GB](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16883360953?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_is-your-gaming-pc-ready-for-gta-6) gets the memory decisions right where it matters. The 16GB version of the 5060 Ti, 32GB of DDR5-6400, and twenty cores with 33MB of L3 behind it. The card is a 1080p-to-1440p part rather than a 4K one, and the 1TB drive is the thing I would add to, but nothing here is a trap.


A perfectly good machine today. The 8GB card is the part I would think about.


I am including the[ABS Cyclone Aqua with the Core i7-14700F and RTX 5060](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16883360992?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_is-your-gaming-pc-ready-for-gta-6) as the honest counterexample. It is a capable 1080p machine — twenty cores, 32GB of DDR4, a 650W supply with room to grow. But the card carries 8GB, and if your plan is specifically to be ready for a very large 2027 open-world port at 1440p, that is the spec I would trade up on. Buy it for what you play now, and treat the graphics card as the upgrade you will make later.


## What I Would Do Today


Nothing urgent. There is no PC date, and hardware bought a year before a release is a year older when the release happens. If you are buying a machine anyway, weight it toward video memory, a large-cache processor and storage rather than raw graphics card tier, because those are the parts of a Rockstar open world that have historically hurt. The current lineup is on Newegg’s[ABS gaming desktop listings](https://www.newegg.com/p/pl?d=ABS+Gaming+Desktop&utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_is-your-gaming-pc-ready-for-gta-6) .


## Frequently Asked Questions


**Is GTA 6 coming to PC?** Rockstar has not announced a PC version. The game is currently scheduled for release on 19 November 2026 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and Series S, and as of September 2026 no Windows release has been dated. Rockstar has historically brought its open-world titles to PC after the console launch, but that is a pattern rather than a commitment.


**When did previous Rockstar games reach PC?** Grand Theft Auto V launched on consoles on 17 September 2013 and on Windows on 14 April 2015. Red Dead Redemption 2 launched on consoles on 26 October 2018 and on Windows on 5 November 2019. Those gaps are roughly nineteen and twelve months respectively.


**What are the GTA 6 PC system requirements?** They have not been published, because no PC version has been announced. Any specific requirement list circulating now is speculation. The sensible approach is to build around what large open-world games have historically demanded rather than an invented specification.


**Is 8GB of video memory enough for upcoming AAA games?** It is workable at 1080p and will likely remain so with adjusted settings, but it is the spec most likely to force compromises in large, texture-heavy releases. Since video memory cannot be added to a graphics card after purchase, 12GB is the floor I would suggest for 1440p and 16GB for anything above.


**Should I buy a gaming PC now or wait for GTA 6?** If you want a machine for the games you play today, buy it now — hardware bought early is simply older by the time an unannounced port arrives. If your only reason to upgrade is GTA 6 on PC, waiting is reasonable, because there is no date to plan around and prices and hardware will both have moved by then.
